narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Class Behind Glass"**

The site is a night-time Royal room where the words of a programming class (KÓD, JEGYZET, PROJEKT, VÁLTOZÁS) drift past at poster scale, and you read about MeetCoder through tinted glass laid over them. One kinetic Allo headline opens each page: letters land on a spring, swell in weight and roundness under the pointer, and carry small stickers set into the line like part of the word. Below it the page moves in fields that rise like the next swatch in a sample book: Royal glass, one Acid Lime field, a deep Royal field, then the night footer sheet.

Density is calm and editorial: few panels, generous gutters, spec rows instead of feature cards. Acid Lime is the counter hue and it means *you*: your download, your project, your platform, your focus. Roundness is meaning as well: Allo's ROND axis stays sharp while something is in progress and goes fully round when it resolves or when you touch it.

This file covers the website (`site/`) only. The native macOS and Windows app has its own system and is out of scope here.
keyCharacteristics: Royal Night ground, Royal tinted glass, Acid Lime as the counter hue.
One kinetic display line per page, with lime and ink stickers inline.
Giant drifting class words behind the glass, never in front of it.
ROND as meaning: sharp at work, round when resolved or touched.
One overshoot spring for everything that lands or responds.
Spec rows and hairlines instead of cards; pills for every action.

rules.name: The Lime Is You Rule
rules.body: On Royal ground, Acid Lime marks the visitor and their own things only: the headline sticker, the arrow chip inside every pill, focus and selection, the "A te projekted" pane and its new files and lines, and the "Ezt használod" OS chip. If an element is about the teacher, the class or the product, it is not lime.

rules.name: The Hue Swap Rule
rules.body: Each field sets `--tint`, `--ink`, `--ring` and `--counter-ink` together (`hue-royal`, `hue-nitro`). Inside the lime field the ring and counter flip to Royal. Never set one of those without the others.

rules.name: The Hairline From Ink Rule
rules.body: Borders and dividers are the local ink at low opacity, so they follow the field they sit in.

rules.name: The ROND Means Done Rule
rules.body: Sharp (ROND 0 to 10) while something is working, fully round (ROND 100) when it resolves or answers a touch. The live-class headline rounds when the class finishes, pills and the undo button round on hover, and display letters round under the pointer.

rules.name: The One Kinetic Line Rule
rules.body: Each page gets one kinetic display headline, split into per-letter spans for the axis effect, and it always keeps a screen-reader label with the plain sentence.

rules.name: The No Drift On Phones Rule
rules.body: At 560px and below nothing drifts, and the world panels render as solid Royal gradients with no `backdrop-filter`. Too little shows through glass at that width to justify it.

rules.name: The Glass Only Over Motion Rule
rules.body: Glass (`backdrop-filter`) is used only where something moves behind it: drift, page content under the nav, a field under a pill. Where nothing moves behind a panel, it is solid.

rules.name: The Transform-Only Glass Rule
rules.body: Glass panels enter with scale and translate only. Opacity or filter on a glass element, or on an ancestor of one, cuts it off from what it frosts.

rules.name: The Flat Inside Rule
rules.body: Inside a glass panel, regions are flat and divided by hairlines. Only code wells (the teacher screen, your local file, commands, shells) are sunken, filled with Royal Night or Royal at 50%.

dos: **Do** keep lime on Royal limited to the visitor: stickers, pill arrow chips, focus and selection, "A te projekted", "Ezt használod".
**Do** switch a field with `hue-royal` or `hue-nitro` so tint, ink, ring and counter-ink change together.
**Do** use spec rows and hairlines (local ink at 16%) where another system would use a row of cards.
**Do** animate glass with `scale` and `translate` only, and give every glass panel a solid fallback (phones at 560px and below, reduced transparency).
**Do** use the spring for anything that lands, lifts or rounds, and Out for color and fades.
**Do** carry state on the ROND axis: sharp while working, round when resolved or touched.
**Do** label demo data with the Példa tag.
donts: **Don't** animate opacity or filter on a glass panel or any ancestor of one; it breaks `backdrop-filter`.
**Don't** use glass where nothing moves behind it; use the solid panel.
**Don't** raise or shadow regions inside a glass panel; only code wells sink.
**Don't** run the drift on phones (560px and below), or put drift in front of content.
**Don't** use lime for the teacher, the class or the product on Royal ground.
**Don't** set more than one kinetic display line per page, or more than one lime field per page.
**Don't** use a second typeface for display or UI; monospace is for code, paths and commands only.
